summary: ECC publishes GateGuard evaluations with runnable harnesses and committed aggregate results. Its pre-registered confirmatory run (run-intent.js, 96 trials) reports the gate's benefit as not confirmed (25/48 passed with the gate against 18/48 without, p = 0.210) at about 37% more turns and 40% more cost per trial; an earlier exploratory run gave 15/24 against 8/24 (p = 0.065). The replay and latency scripts report denials falling from 157 to 132 and must-deny bypasses from 8 to 0 on a 184-step corpus, and a fresh-process hook p50 of 23.68 ms against 11.58 ms on upstream/main; row-level results and transcripts of the hidden-intent runs are not committed. Outside GateGuard, the README's '~60% cost reduction' for defaulting to Sonnet is stated without data, and the mgrep '~2x fewer tokens' figure is attributed to Mixedbread.
